stack_detection.signature: single CANVAS element covering the viewport; DOM has no text/interactive nodes inside it

cells.channel_setup: Chromium via CDP; DOMSnapshot distilled view.

t1_read_text.detail: Score/level text is drawn INTO the canvas; structured view sees none of it. But it does not lie: it emits exactly '[pixels] canvas 0,0,1280,800' — the whole screen declared as one opaque region. Agent must fall back to vision on that rect.

t2_enumerate.detail: No enumerable elements — correctly reported as one opaque canvas, not a fabricated tree.

t4_living_screen.detail: A real game would animate; the structured channel would keep declaring the same opaque rect (no free change signal) — pixels/diffing of the crop is the only option.

t5_blind_action.detail: No coordinates derivable from structure; aiming requires vision on the crop.

t6_pictorial.detail: THE key safety result: the opaque region is DECLARED with its exact rect. Failure is explicit, not silent — a router can detect 'structure covers 0% of this screen' before acting and switch to the pixel path.

measurements.notes: This is the wanted NEGATIVE that proves the perimeter law and the safety property simultaneously: where structure yields nothing (games, video, remote desktop), it says so explicitly. Full-screen canvas apps (games, some Google Docs modes) collapse to the pixel baseline — no gain, but no silent loss either.

runtime_verification.method: compare structured view coverage to screenshot content
runtime_verification.agreement: structured view explicitly covers 0% of on-screen content and declares it (opaque rect) — consistent, not divergent

cells.app: Chromium / Chrome DevTools Protocol (covers all Electron apps: VS Code, Slack, Discord, Teams)

stack_detection.signature: --remote-debugging-port responds on the target process (Electron apps expose the same)

cells.channel_setup: CDP: DOMSnapshot.captureSnapshot (distilled semantic view) + LayerTree (paint ops). See parent repo src/capture.mjs.

t1_read_text.detail: Full visible text as real strings (no glyph decoding), plus off-viewport content. Verified in phase-1 grounding eval (4/4) on randomized data.

t2_enumerate.detail: Interactive elements with roles, boxes, ids, live input values; whole page not just viewport.

t4_living_screen.detail: Structured diffs: 14 tok (toast fade) to 205 tok (table reflow); 0 on idle; living feed 6 s = 587 tok vs 8196 screenshot (14x).

t5_blind_action.detail: Coordinates from the view drove raw CDP Input clicks onto correct targets (phase-1 eval 4/4).

t6_pictorial.detail: img/canvas declared as [pixels] rects; targeted crops interpreted by vision (visual eval 3/3, 3/3). Opaque regions are explicit, never silent.

measurements.notes: Reference numbers from phase-1 (results/representations.json, diffs.json). App-UI structured view 308 tok vs 1366 screenshot (4.4x); capture 3-5 ms vs ~120 ms. This is the highest-coverage general channel because it covers the entire Chromium/Electron share of the desktop cross-OS with identical method.

runtime_verification.method: grounding eval (4/4) + visual eval (3/3 x2), mechanical
runtime_verification.agreement: structured view + declared crops fully consistent with screen

stack_detection.signature: org.a11y.Bus not activatable in headless sandbox; app does not register

cells.channel_setup: Attempted: dbus-run-session + at-spi-bus-launcher + at-spi2-registryd, then Atspi.init()/get_desktop walk via gi.repository.Atspi.

t1_read_text.detail: Not reachable: AT-SPI client failed with 'A connection to the bus can't be made' — org.a11y.Bus is not provided without a real login session; xdg portals also fail (no display/seat). GTK4 also rejects legacy GTK_A11Y=atspi (GTK4 auto-registers only when a session a11y bus exists).

measurements.notes: Environmental block, NOT a property of AT-SPI itself. On a real logged-in Linux desktop AT-SPI is the standard cross-toolkit channel and is expected to work (the Linux agent brief covers it there). Recorded here because it is a genuine predictability datum: AT-SPI depends on a full session bus, so it is unavailable in headless/CI/server contexts where an agent might run — a routing consideration for production.

permissions_required: a logged-in session bus providing org.a11y.Bus

stack_detection.method: mapped shared libraries of the target process
stack_detection.signature: libgtk-4.so.1 mapped; renderer submits via gsk_renderer_render()

cells.channel_setup: gdb tap on gsk_renderer_render calling gsk_render_node_serialize in-process (LD_PRELOAD defeated by libgtk -Bsymbolic build; documented). GSK_RENDERER=cairo.

t1_read_text.detail: Known file content recovered exactly by decoding GSK text-node glyph IDs via reverse cmap: 'The quick brown fox 12345', 'RENDER-TAP-SENTINEL-XYZ', plus chrome 'Open','known.txt','/tmp'. Text arrives as glyph IDs (post-HarfBuzz), decoded one-table-per-font.

t2_enumerate.detail: Tree exposes container/transform/border/text nodes with bounds; header buttons (Open, new-tab, menu, window controls) present as distinct subtrees with geometry.

t3_live_value.detail: Editor text shown is the live document content (not a placeholder); a second frame after load reflects the buffer.

t4_living_screen.detail: Static editor; living-screen economics already measured on widget-factory (~1-2 KB inter-frame diff during animation). Not re-run here.

t5_blind_action.detail: Not dispatched under broadway headless in this pass; GTK bounds are exact (see re-render), coordinates are directly usable. Deferred to interactive session.

t6_pictorial.detail: No image in this doc; texture nodes (when present) embed their bitmap in the tree and are declarable as opaque rects (verified on widget-factory photo).

measurements.notes: Serialized frame 16 KB (1.7 KB texture, 14.3 KB verbose pre-distillation structure). Naive token count high because serialization is verbose CSS-like text; distillation (as in browser DOM view) would cut this sharply. The load-bearing facts here are completeness + text recovery, not raw token count.

runtime_verification.method: re-render intercepted tree with gtk4-rendernode-tool, compare to on-screen frame
runtime_verification.agreement: exact: re-rendered PNG is the editor window pixel-for-pixel (artifacts/linux-gnome-text-editor-rerender.png)

permissions_required: ability to attach gdb to own child process (ptrace)

stack_detection.signature: soffice.bin running; UNO endpoint 'socket,port=2002;urp' accepts a connection

t1_read_text.detail: Document text read exactly, including accents: 'UNO-SENTINEL-ALPHA\nLigne deux avec accents: éàü and number 98765\nTroisième paragraphe.' This is the document model itself — above any render tree; text is real strings, no glyph decoding needed.

t2_enumerate.detail: UNO exposes the full object model (paragraphs, tables, frames, shapes, form controls) with enumerable structure and geometry; richer than a render tree for document semantics.

t3_live_value.detail: getString() reflects the live in-memory document; edits are visible immediately via the same API.

t4_living_screen.detail: N/A for a static document; UNO is event/model-based, not frame-based.

t5_blind_action.detail: UNO can both locate (view cursor -> screen coords) and act directly via the model (insert/format) — actuation need not go through pixels at all.

t6_pictorial.detail: Embedded images/shapes are enumerable objects with bounds and, for images, the bitmap — declarable and extractable; not silently lost.

measurements.notes: Object-model text for this page = ~21 tokens vs ~1366 for a page screenshot (~65x). Strongest positive class in the study: when the app exposes its document model, the render tree is unnecessary. Linux analog of Windows Word-via-COM.

runtime_verification.method: known sentinel string typed into source doc, checked against getString()

permissions_required: local socket connection to own soffice instance

cells.channel_setup: Investigated whether Qt exposes a serializable render tree analogous to GTK's gsk_render_node_serialize().

t1_read_text.detail: No public render-tree serialization exists in Qt. QWidget apps paint via QPainter into a backing store (pixels); Qt Quick composes a GPU scene graph (QSG) that is internal with no text-dump API. Unlike GTK there is no one-call tree export. The render-tap channel is therefore not available for Qt.

t2_enumerate.detail: Not via render tap. Qt's semantic channel is AT-SPI (if the app enables QAccessible) — see the accessibility-api cell; blocked in this headless sandbox but the correct route on a real session.

measurements.notes: Documented architectural refusal — the contrast with GTK is a core finding: the render-tap approach is toolkit-dependent, not universal. GTK exposes gsk_render_node_serialize(); Qt exposes nothing equivalent. For Qt the only structured channel is AT-SPI (semantic API), which sidesteps the render level entirely. This is exactly the 'predictability' story: the available channel is a function of the toolkit signature, knowable in advance, but coverage varies sharply by toolkit.
